gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much power these small stations use while sitting idle over a weekend. The Technology Man measured the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 losing about 11 W with DC on and Eco mode off (100% down to 24% in 20 h), so in that state it would empty itself in about a day. The Solar Lab measured the EcoFlow TRAIL 300 DC using only about 2 Wh in 24 h while switched on and powering nothing.
standout_why: I checked against the two pages ChatGPT cited, The Gadgeteer's C300 DC review and the manuals.plus C300 DC guide, plus Amphourly's 'Best Small Portable Power Stations', which ranked in the top results. The Gadgeteer only says it saw 'no measurable idle draw' on the C300 DC, gives no figure, and covers no other model. The manuals.plus guide lists specs only. Amphourly says its usable Wh is a calculation (85% of rated capacity) and that runtimes are estimates, with no measurements. I couldn't open GearRanking's C300 DC 'tested capacity' page (certificate error), so I can't rule out that it has a capacity figure. None of these pages gives an idle-drain number, or a delivered-Wh number taken at a 100 W USB-C load. It scores 2, not 3, because the Elite 30 V2's drain can be avoided by turning Eco mode on or switching DC off.
decides: This confirms the DC-only units, the EcoFlow TRAIL 300 DC and the Anker SOLIX C300 DC, as the safer weekend picks. TRAIL 300 DC: about 2 Wh a day idle (The Solar Lab). Anker C300X DC, the EU sister model: 269.65 Wh delivered at USB-C 20 V/5 A, the 100 W laptop condition (techtest.org), so about 4.5 charges of a 60 Wh laptop. The BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 needs a caveat if it stays on our page. The Technology Man measured about 11 W of DC drain with Eco mode off, and MacRumors saw about 10% gone in 4 h with DC on. So the page should tell readers to turn Eco mode on or switch DC off between charges, or move the Elite 30 V2 down the list. The EcoFlow RIVER 3 delivered only 210 Wh in StorageReview's test (AC fan load). The Jackery 240 v2 delivered 219 Wh on DC in The Technology Man's test. Both are a step below the 288 Wh units.

findings.label: Idle drain with DC output on, Eco mode off (The Technology Man)
findings.source_title: This £189 Bluetti Elite 30 V2 Power Station Is Better Than I Expected (Gidon, The Technology Man, 23 Dec 2025)
findings.note: Measured by the reviewer. 76% of 288 Wh = 219 Wh over 20 h, about 11 W. Over a 48 h weekend that would be about 525 Wh, more than the whole battery, so DC must be off or Eco mode on between charges. With AC on and Eco off the same review measured 100% to 19% in 12 h (about 19 W).

findings.label: Usable energy delivered, DC and AC (The Technology Man)
findings.value: 244 Wh on DC (about 85%); 231 Wh on AC (about 80%)
findings.source_title: This £189 Bluetti Elite 30 V2 Power Station Is Better Than I Expected (Gidon, The Technology Man, 23 Dec 2025)
findings.note: Constant-load full discharge. The review doesn't give the load wattage. It also measured both USB-C ports maxed together at almost 240 W combined.

findings.label: Battery drop with DC on, plus MacBook Air charges (MacRumors)
findings.value: about 10% in 4 h with DC on; 3.5 MacBook Air charges
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 30 V2 Portable Power Station Review (Juli Clover, MacRumors, 4 Dec 2025)
findings.note: 10% of 288 Wh = 28.8 Wh over 4 h, about 7 W, which is in line with The Technology Man's figure. Our page already quotes the 3.5 charges; the drain figure is new.

findings.label: Idle drain while switched on, nothing connected (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow TRAIL 300 DC Review: Tiny, Tough, and Surprisingly Long-Lasting (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The page shows no author or publication date, only a © 2026 footer. Same review: charging through both USB-C ports took roughly 1 h, and about 15 iPhone 16 Pro Max charges. It gives no Wh-delivered figure.

findings.product: Anker SOLIX C300X DC (EU sister of the C300 DC)
findings.label: Energy delivered over USB-C at 20 V/5 A, i.e. 100 W (techtest.org)
findings.value: 269.65 Wh (94% of 288 Wh); average across 5 loads 272.9 Wh
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C300X DC im Test (Michael Barton, techtest.org, 21 May 2026)
findings.note: Other loads: USB-C 9V/3A 271.45 Wh; USB-C 28V/5A 273.08 Wh; 12V/2A 277.6 Wh; 12V/10A 272.8 Wh. Weighed at 2.88 kg. This is the C300X DC, not the US C300 DC (A1722); techtest calls it a DC-only sister of the C300. Arithmetic: 269.65 / 60 Wh laptop battery = about 4.5 charges, before the laptop's own charging losses.

findings.label: Idle draw (techtest.org)
findings.value: about 2.3 W with all ports off; 12.6 W with AC outlets on; usable 253.8 Wh average (214–271.7 Wh)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C300 Test (Michael Barton, techtest.org, 26 Nov 2024)
findings.note: This is the AC model, weighed at 4.1 kg, not the DC model. The worst result (214 Wh) came from a low AC load. Shown to illustrate the inverter-on penalty, not as a C300 DC figure.

findings.label: Real laptop use over several days (The Gadgeteer)
findings.value: Station 100% → 70% after 24 h with an M1 MacBook Pro plugged in and in use, then 46%, 21%, 7% on the following three days. Charging the laptop from 27% to 80% used about 15% of the station.
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C300 DC Portable Power Station review (The Gadgeteer, 26 Nov 2024)
findings.note: A ChatGPT-cited rival page, so not new. Included to compare with the drain figures above. The reviewer reported no measurable idle draw but gave no number.

findings.label: Full discharge, recharge energy, charge draw (StorageReview)
findings.value: 210 Wh delivered (rated 245 Wh); 270 Wh from the wall to recharge; 322 W charge draw
findings.source_title: EcoFlow River 3 Review (Corinne OBrien, StorageReview, 7 Oct 2024)
findings.note: Load was a 300 W fan on AC, not USB-C, so the 100 W USB-C figure would likely be somewhat higher. Arithmetic: 210 / 60 Wh = about 3.5 laptop charges.

findings.label: Usable energy, standby drain and USB-C laptop charging (The Technology Man)
findings.value: 219 Wh on DC (8 A, about 92 W; 86%); 193 Wh on AC (75%); about 4%/h drain with AC on and nothing connected; MacBook Pro charged at over 90 W over USB-C
findings.source_title: Power All Your Tech Anywhere: Jackery Explorer 240 V2 Full Review (Gidon, The Technology Man, 14 Nov 2024)
findings.note: 4% of 256 Wh per hour is about 10 W with the inverter on. The reviewer says the DC drain is 'far smaller' but gives no figure. Weighed at 3.8 kg.
